In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IFN β activates two distinct responses in which the U-ISGF response is critical for the prolonged resistance to viruses and to DNA damage.
the prolonged response to IFNβ is mediated by unphosphorylation ISGF3 (U-ISGF3) and that the U-ISFG3-dependent genes play a role in antiviral defense and in therapy resistance.
U-ISGF3 is the key mediator for IFN β -mediated prolonged resistance to viruses and to DNA damage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IFN β has a biphasic effect on cancer cells: the initial response to IFNs is to induce cytotoxic genes, which kill cancer cells.
the U-ISG response to IFN is a powerful and prolonged antiviral response, but also promotes cancer therapy resistance.
IFN β induces two distinct responses, the rapid and transient ISGF3-dependent response and the prolonged ISGF3-independent U-ISGF3 response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IFN β induces a second phase of response, which is mediated by U-ISGF3 and is critical for prolonged antiviral effects but also leads to DNA damage and cancer resistance.
the prolonged second phase IFN response, mediated by U-ISGF3, is critical in the antiviral response, and also in the resistance to cancer therapy.
the IFN β -mediated response to DNA damage is not only dependent on STAT1 and IRFs 7 and 9, but also STAT2 and IRF9.
